column3: -x filters on the exact fstype (probed 9.4): GNU under WSL sits on ext4, so -x ntfs excludes nothing and prints the mount table rc 0; the Windows sides see NTFS (also case-distinct from ntfs) and print their volume table rc 0 — rc parity holds, stdout is the platform-inherent listing (value model), recorded not compared.

The `ln -s . l` operand needs Windows Developer Mode; without it the symlink does not exist and df reports l missing (rc 1), while GNU resolves the symlink to its mount and prints the table (rc 0). Platform-bound symlink creation, recorded not gated.
